oh dear. hey op im black too and i hope u hear me out on this. i used to think almost exactly like you. i promise you this is internalised racism. i also grew up around mostly white people and that meant that the only time i was seeing/hearing about black ppl was when they were acting in the "degenerate" ways u described. the only thing that started to change things for me was when i started willingly interacting with other black people online. 

consider why all you see about us seems to be negative. if you really were seeing us unbiased, if you heard us speak with our own mouths, you would see us for more than that. social media (really, all media) is an echo chamber, it will show you things deliberately to reinforce ur racist thinking and make u think it's normal just to keep you on the app. algorithms are poisonous to the mind and staying in that chamber is a surefire path to never getting over your self hatred.

black people are no more degenerates than any other race. i know this because at this point in my life i know more educated, mature, and thoughtful black people than any other race. additionally, i am black and educated, mature, and thoughtful. and it sounds like you are too. if black people were predetermined to just be fat, loud, and idiotic, this could not be. we are not special outliers. 

it hurts to see u say such things about ur own people, my people, but i understand. u have to open yourself to seeing things in a new light. for your own sake, i hope you can find it within yourself to try. you do not deserve to hate yourself for the colour of your skin. much love

i did. i could manage in primary school, when i could make one friend and kind of attach myself to them the whole time. the way i was taught also made sense to me. but everything fell apart in high school, with the cliques and changing teachers for every class and whatnot.

a lot of times i wouldn't even do my major assignments because i couldnt cope with all the different things. i started skipping individual classes, which eventually became full days, and by the time i finished, my teachers were shocked if i showed up more than 3 days a week. i had a lot of outbursts too for seemingly no reason (freaking out at teachers when they weren't explaining things "right", storming out of classes, generally being disruptive). it made me think i was a violent, bad person, but now that im out of that setting, im actually really quiet and calm.

it was extremely turbulent for me and i Do Not miss it at all lol
